title: Prediction-Intervention Games and Invariant Sets
abstract: arXiv:2605.16828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We consider the following two-player game: using observational data, the leader chooses a prediction function for a response variable $Y$ from given covariates. The follower then reacts with an intervention on some covariates in the underlying structural causal model to maximize their own objective. The leader knows the intervention targets, but may have limited knowledge of the follower's objective. We call this setup a prediction-intervention game, a special case of a Stackelberg game. Finding an optimal strategy for the leader is generally difficult. To avoid severe performance loss, the leader may base their prediction on the causal parents of $Y$, or more generally on an invariant subset of covariates. We prove, for two common classes of follower objectives, that predictors based on the stable blanket, an invariant subset, are at least as good as those based on the causal parents. translated_title: 预测-干预博弈与不变集
translated_abstract: 我们考虑以下双人博弈：领导者利用观测数据，从给定协变量中为响应变量 $Y$ 选择一个预测函数。随后，跟随者通过对底层结构因果模型中的某些协变量进行干预来做出反应，以最大化自身的目标。领导者知道干预的目标变量，但对跟随者的目标可能了解有限。我们将这种设定称为预测-干预博弈，它是Stackelberg博弈的一种特例。寻找领导者的最优策略通常是困难的。为避免严重的性能损失，领导者可以将其预测建立在 $Y$ 的因果父节点之上，或更一般地建立在协变量的某个不变子集之上。我们证明，对于两类常见的跟随者目标，基于稳定毯（一种不变子集）的预测器至少与基于因果父节点的预测器一样好。我们进一步对领导者干预后……
tldr: 该论文提出预测-干预博弈（Stackelberg博弈的特例），并证明对于两类常见的跟随者干预目标，基于稳定毯这一不变子集的预测器性能至少与基于因果父节点的预测器相当。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces prediction-intervention games, a special case of Stackelberg games, and proves that for two common classes of follower objectives, predictors based on the stable blanket—an invariant subset of covariates—are at least as good as those based on causal parents.
